steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Evolutionary explanations: NVC evolved because it helped survival. Darwin argued that facial expressions evolved from useful actions (e.g. baring teeth in anger originally prepared for biting). Universal expressions suggest an evolutionary origin shared across cultures.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Innate explanations: NVC is biologically programmed. Evidence: Ekman's universal facial expressions; blind individuals show similar facial expressions despite never seeing them (Matsumoto & Hwang); infants smile and cry without learning.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Cultural explanations: NVC is learned through socialisation. Evidence: display rules vary across cultures; specific gestures (emblems) have different meanings in different cultures; proxemics vary by culture (Latin American cultures use less space than Northern European).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Yuki's study (2007): compared how American and Japanese participants interpreted emotional expressions using eyes vs mouths. Japanese participants relied more on eyes (cultural emphasis on reading subtle eye cues in a collectivist culture), while Americans relied more on mouths. This demonstrates that NVC interpretation is culturally shaped.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Compare evolutionary and cultural explanations of non-verbal behaviour. | Describe Yuki's study on cultural differences in interpreting facial expressions and evaluate its methodology. | Discuss whether non-verbal behaviour is primarily innate or learned.
